title: A product theorem for $r$-cross intersecting families of subspaces
summary: Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over a finite field of order $q$. Let $r\geq 3$, $(r-1)n\geq rk$ and let $\mathcal F_1,\ldots,\mathcal F_r\subset \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{V}{k}$, where $\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{V}{k}$ denotes the set of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $V$. Suppose that $F_1\cap\cdots\cap F_r\neq\{0\}$ holds for all $F_i\in\mathcal F_i$, $1\leq i\leq r$. Then we show that $\prod_{i=1}^r|\mathcal F_i|\leq\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n-1}{k-1}$, provided $n-k$ is sufficiently large for fixed $q$ and $r$.
